categories.name: Matthew
categories.description: Jesus as the promised King, fulfilling the Scriptures

categories.name: Mark
categories.description: The fast-paced account of Jesus as the suffering servant

categories.name: Luke
categories.description: The careful, compassionate account of Jesus' life

categories.name: John
categories.description: Jesus as the divine Son of God, told through signs

quizQuestions.prompt: Matthew's Gospel opens with a genealogy tracing Jesus' lineage back to which patriarch?
quizQuestions.explanation: Matthew 1 traces Jesus' genealogy back to Abraham, emphasizing His place in Israel's story.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who visited baby Jesus bringing gold, frankincense, and myrrh, following a star, according to Matthew?
quizQuestions.explanation: Wise men (Magi) from the East visited, guided by a star, bringing these gifts.

quizQuestions.prompt: What horrific order did King Herod give after being deceived by the wise men?
quizQuestions.explanation: Herod ordered the slaughter of male infants in and around Bethlehem.

options.text: The slaughter of infant boys in Bethlehem
The exile of all Jewish priests
The arrest of the wise men

quizQuestions.prompt: What two everyday images did Jesus use to describe His followers in the Sermon on the Mount?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus called His followers "the salt of the earth" and "the light of the world."

options.text: Salt of the earth and light of the world

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Judas do after realizing his betrayal had led to Jesus' condemnation?
quizQuestions.explanation: Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver and hanged himself.

options.text: Returned the silver and hanged himself

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jesus command His disciples in the Great Commission at the end of Matthew, regarding baptism?
quizQuestions.explanation: He told them to baptize "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

options.text: Baptize in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost

quizQuestions.prompt: Which royal line does Matthew's genealogy especially emphasize, presenting Jesus as Israel's promised ruler?
quizQuestions.explanation: Matthew highlights Jesus' descent through the line of King David.

options.text: The line of the priests of Levi

quizQuestions.prompt: Which audience is Matthew's Gospel traditionally understood to have been written primarily for?
quizQuestions.explanation: Matthew is traditionally seen as written for a Jewish audience, emphasizing fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Matthew's account of the crucifixion, what happened to the Temple veil at the moment Jesus died?
quizQuestions.explanation: The veil of the Temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.

options.text: It was torn in two, from top to bottom
It was removed by the priests

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the Roman guards do after the resurrection, according to Matthew's unique account of the tomb's guards?
quizQuestions.explanation: The guards were paid by the chief priests to spread a false story that the disciples stole Jesus' body.

options.text: Were paid to spread a false story about the disciples
Reported the truth to Pilate immediately
Were executed for failing their duty

quizQuestions.prompt: In the Sermon on the Mount, what did Jesus teach His listeners, encouraging them to trust in daily provision rather than being consumed by their own concerns?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus taught not to worry, pointing to how God cares for the birds of the air and the lilies of the field.

options.text: Not to worry, since God cares for birds and flowers
To store up food for hard times
To avoid nature and focus on the Temple

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Pilate famously do before condemning Jesus, symbolizing he wanted no part in the decision?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pilate washed his hands before the crowd, declaring himself innocent of Jesus' blood.

options.text: Washed his hands before the crowd

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Matthew 27:19, what did Pilate's wife send him during Jesus' trial, urging him not to condemn an innocent man?
quizQuestions.explanation: She sent word that she had suffered in a dream because of Jesus, urging Pilate to have nothing to do with "that just man."

options.text: A dream warning him to leave Jesus alone
A message that Jesus had escaped
A demand to execute Jesus quickly
An invitation to visit the Temple

quizQuestions.prompt: What group of religious leaders does Matthew frequently show in conflict with Jesus over legalistic interpretations of the Law?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Pharisees repeatedly clashed with Jesus over legalistic traditions.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Matthew record Jesus teaching about forgiveness, when Peter asked how many times to forgive?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus told Peter to forgive "seventy times seven," meaning without limit.

quizQuestions.prompt: What final promise does Jesus make to His disciples in the closing verse of Matthew's Gospel?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world."

options.text: "I am with you always, even to the end of the world"

quizQuestions.prompt: Mark's Gospel is traditionally understood to be based on the eyewitness account of which apostle?
quizQuestions.explanation: Early church tradition holds that Mark recorded the preaching of Peter.

quizQuestions.prompt: Unlike Matthew and Luke, what does Mark's Gospel skip entirely at its start?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mark has no birth narrative, opening instead with John the Baptist's ministry.

quizQuestions.prompt: What word does Mark's Gospel repeatedly use to move quickly between events, giving it a fast pace?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mark frequently uses "immediately" (or "straightway"), reflecting its urgent, action-driven style.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the Roman centurion declare after witnessing how Jesus died on the cross, in Mark's account?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Truly this man was the Son of God."

options.text: "Truly this man was the Son of God"

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Jesus doing in the boat, according to Mark, right before He calmed the storm?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus was asleep on a pillow in the stern of the boat.

quizQuestions.prompt: At Caesarea Philippi in Mark 8, what did Peter declare Jesus to be when asked "whom say ye that I am"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter answered, "Thou art the Christ."

quizQuestions.prompt: What event on a mountain did Peter, James, and John witness, where Jesus' appearance changed and Moses and Elijah appeared?
quizQuestions.explanation: This event is called the Transfiguration.

quizQuestions.prompt: What odd detail does Mark alone record about someone fleeing the scene when Jesus was arrested?
quizQuestions.explanation: A young man fled naked, leaving his linen cloth behind when seized.

options.text: A young man fled naked, leaving his garment behind
A soldier dropped his sword and ran
A disciple hid in a nearby house

quizQuestions.prompt: Which audience is Mark's Gospel traditionally thought to have been written primarily for?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mark is traditionally seen as written for a Roman/Gentile audience, given its fast pace and explanation of Jewish customs.

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Mark's book open, declaring something directly about Jesus in its very first verse?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God."

options.text: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God"
"The book of the generation of Jesus Christ"
"Forasmuch as many have taken in hand"

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Mark 10:45, what did Jesus say He came to do, describing His mission as a servant?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many."

options.text: To serve and give His life as a ransom

quizQuestions.prompt: What poor widow's offering did Jesus praise in the Temple, in Mark 12, though it was worth very little in money?
quizQuestions.explanation: A poor widow gave two small coins, all she had to live on, which Jesus praised above the rich givers.

options.text: Two small coins, all she had

quizQuestions.prompt: What teaching about the Sabbath did Jesus give in Mark 2:27, explaining its true purpose?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath."

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notable about the pace and length of Mark's Gospel compared to the other three Gospels?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mark is the shortest of the four Gospels and moves at the fastest, most action-driven pace.

options.text: It is the shortest and fastest-paced
It is the longest of the four
It is written entirely in poetry
It has the most parables of the four

quizQuestions.prompt: To whom does Luke address his Gospel in its opening verses?
quizQuestions.explanation: Luke addresses his account to Theophilus.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Luke's profession, according to Paul's description of him elsewhere in the New Testament?
quizQuestions.explanation: Colossians 4:14 calls Luke "the beloved physician."

quizQuestions.prompt: What were the shepherds doing when angels announced Jesus' birth to them, in Luke's account?
quizQuestions.explanation: They were watching their flocks by night in the fields.

quizQuestions.prompt: What song of praise did Mary sing after learning she would bear Jesus, recorded only in Luke?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mary's song, known as the Magnificat, begins "My soul doth magnify the Lord."

options.text: The Magnificat ("My soul doth magnify the Lord")

quizQuestions.prompt: At what age did the boy Jesus stay behind in Jerusalem, found discussing Scripture with the Temple teachers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus was twelve years old when this happened.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, whose story appears only in Luke?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zacchaeus climbed a sycamore tree because he was too short to see over the crowd.

quizQuestions.prompt: After His resurrection, Jesus appeared to two disciples walking to which village, though they didn't recognize Him at first?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus walked with them to Emmaus, and they recognized Him when He broke bread.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which elderly priest was struck mute for doubting the angel's announcement that his wife would bear John the Baptist?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah (Zacharias) was struck mute until John's birth.

quizQuestions.prompt: Unlike Matthew, whose genealogy of Jesus does Luke's genealogy trace all the way back to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Luke's genealogy traces back to Adam, emphasizing Jesus' connection to all humanity.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which other New Testament book did the author of Luke also write, as a sequel about the early church?
quizQuestions.explanation: Luke also wrote the Acts of the Apostles.

quizQuestions.prompt: What Roman order caused Joseph and Mary to travel to Bethlehem, according to Luke?
quizQuestions.explanation: A census/taxation decree from Caesar Augustus required everyone to register in their ancestral town.

options.text: A census decree by Caesar Augustus

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jesus promise the repentant criminal crucified beside Him, according to Luke?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Today shalt thou be with me in paradise."

options.text: "Today shalt thou be with me in paradise"
"Thy sins are too great to forgive"

quizQuestions.prompt: Which two sisters did Jesus visit, where one sat listening to Him while the other was busy serving?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mary sat at Jesus' feet listening, while Martha was busy with household duties.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did the angel Gabriel tell Mary would happen, to explain how she would conceive Jesus?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Holy Ghost would come upon her, and the power of the Highest would overshadow her.

options.text: The Holy Ghost would come upon her
She would travel to Egypt first
An angel would raise the child

quizQuestions.prompt: In Luke 4, Jesus preached His first recorded sermon in Nazareth, reading from a scroll of which prophet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus read from Isaiah, declaring "this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears."

quizQuestions.prompt: Luke's Gospel is especially known for emphasizing Jesus' compassion toward which groups, more than the other Gospels?
quizQuestions.explanation: Luke highlights Jesus' compassion for the poor, outcasts, women, and Samaritans.

options.text: The poor, outcasts, women, and Samaritans

quizQuestions.prompt: How does John's Gospel uniquely open, describing Jesus before His birth?
quizQuestions.explanation: John opens with "In the beginning was the Word," describing Jesus as the eternal Word who was with God and was God.

options.text: "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ"
"Forasmuch as many have taken in hand"

quizQuestions.prompt: John's Gospel is structured around a series of miraculous signs. About how many major signs are typically counted in John?
quizQuestions.explanation: Scholars typically count seven major signs structuring John's account of Jesus' ministry.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to John 3:16, what did God give because He loved the world?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son."

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jesus do just before raising Lazarus from the dead, showing His human emotion?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Jesus wept" — the shortest verse in the Bible.

quizQuestions.prompt: In John 4, Jesus spoke with a woman at a well in which region, a place Jews typically avoided?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus spoke with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well in Samaria.

quizQuestions.prompt: What humble act of service did Jesus perform for His disciples at the Last Supper, uniquely detailed in John?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus washed His disciples' feet, modeling humble service.

options.text: He served them a full meal alone
He gave them each a gift
He sang a psalm over them

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Thomas require before he would believe Jesus had truly risen from the dead?
quizQuestions.explanation: Thomas said he needed to see and touch Jesus' wounds to believe.

options.text: To see and touch His wounds
To hear a voice from heaven

quizQuestions.prompt: What did John the Baptist call Jesus when he saw Him approaching, according to John 1:29?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does John 20:31 give as the stated purpose for writing his Gospel?
quizQuestions.explanation: "These are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God."

options.text: So readers would believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God
To record a complete history of Rome
To settle a dispute among the apostles
To list every miracle Jesus performed

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notably rare in John's Gospel, compared to Matthew, Mark, and Luke (the Synoptic Gospels)?
quizQuestions.explanation: John contains far fewer parables than the other three Gospels, favoring extended discourses and signs instead.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jesus say to the accusers of a woman caught in adultery, before they all walked away?
quizQuestions.explanation: "He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her."

options.text: "He that is without sin among you, let him cast the first stone"
"She must be judged by the priests"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does John 15:13 say is the greatest expression of love?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends."

options.text: Laying down one's life for a friend

quizQuestions.prompt: Which of Jesus' many "I am" statements in John describes Him providing spiritual nourishment?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am the bread of life" is one of John's several "I am" statements.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which "I am" statement in John describes Jesus as the sole path to the Father?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

options.text: "I am the way, the truth, and the life"

quizQuestions.prompt: In the fourth Gospel's account of the crucifixion, who did Jesus entrust to care for His mother Mary?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus entrusted Mary to the care of "the disciple whom he loved," traditionally understood as John.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to John's Gospel, what happened when a soldier pierced Jesus' side with a spear after His death?
quizQuestions.explanation: Blood and water came out, confirming He was truly dead.
